languageDiagnosisCard.description: Controls how the AI asks, judges and grades in the diagnosis chat. Applies to every workspace. German only for now.
languageDiagnosisCard.hint: Controls the flow, the question style and the output format of the test. Four placeholders in the text are filled in: '{language}' with the language of the test, '{grading}' with the grading rules below, '{levels}' with the descriptions from the Levels A1 to C2 card and '{examples}' with the example sentences from there. A placeholder you delete is appended at the end, so the AI never loses it.

diagnosisPlanCard.title: Language Test questions
diagnosisPlanCard.description: Decides which questions the Language Test asks. Each row is one question with one of two task types. Choice means clicking and needs answer options with at least one marked correct. Free text means typing and needs only the question text. The solution on a free text is optional and decides who marks it: with a solution the code checks the answer word for word, without one the AI judges it at the end. Anything that belongs before the question, a short reading text or an everyday situation, simply goes into the question text. The order is the order in the test and runs from easy to hard. Either you write everything yourself, or you let the AI write it once and read it through. The test itself then runs without a single AI call. The AI assigns the level A1 to C2 at the end from the answers, not per question.
diagnosisPlanCard.languageHint: The test is in German, so questions and options are too.
diagnosisPlanCard.freeTextHint: At least 2 free-text questions without a solution are required. Only those does the AI judge itself, and only they give the level a real writing sample.
diagnosisPlanCard.optionsHint: Mark exactly one correct. Several are allowed if the question says so.
diagnosisPlanCard.answersHint: Leave it empty if the AI should judge the answer. If you enter a solution, the code checks the typed answer and this question needs no AI at all. One solution per line, every line counts as correct. Capitalisation and a final punctuation mark are ignored, accents and umlauts are not. Short solutions give the learner a one-line box, whole sentences the big one.
diagnosisPlanCard.gradedByCodeHint: Checked without AI. The typed answer has to match one of the solutions.
diagnosisPlanCard.gradedByAiHint: The AI judges this answer at the end, using the grading rules and the level examples from the AI behaviour tab. This row counts towards the required writing samples.
diagnosisPlanCard.generate: Let the AI write the questions
diagnosisPlanCard.generatingHint: This takes about a minute. The AI writes a complete set of questions, and you can change every one of them afterwards.

cookies.heading: 3. Cookies

recipients.heading: 4. Recipients
recipients.body:
For AI features and translations, content is sent to services of TH Lübeck (THL myLab), GWDG and DeepL. The platform is operated by Hetzner Online GmbH in Germany.
Embedded YouTube videos load only after a click. Google then receives the IP address and device data, including in the USA.
Teachers can connect their own accounts with external providers. Content then goes to that provider, possibly outside the EU.

retention.heading: 5. Retention
retention.body: Data is kept until the account or the content is deleted, at the latest until the end of the pilot project. Time-limited accounts are deleted after they expire, server logs after a few weeks. On request, we delete earlier.

whatIsKis.q: What is KIS and what is it for?
whatIsKis.a: KIS is a pilot project at TH Lübeck. It brings together two things: the learning assistant, who answers from the materials stored in a workspace, and the services you use to produce teaching material.

vsChatgpt.q: How is the learning assistant different from ChatGPT?
vsChatgpt.a:
The learning assistant is built on RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation): it looks up the matching passages in your workspace's materials and answers only from those, attaching a source to every sentence, which opens the exact spot in the document. Anything beyond that he turns down. The closer comparison is Gemini Notebook by Google (formerly NotebookLM), not ChatGPT.

On top of that, processing runs with providers in Germany, not in the US. Our data is not used for training.

KIS itself is open source under the Apache 2.0 license.

moduleServiceTool.q: What is the difference between a workspace, a service and a tool?
moduleServiceTool.a: A workspace is a course room with materials and chat. A service stands on its own, such as translation or screencast. A tool sits in the studio inside a workspace, such as flashcards or quizzes.

costs.q: Does this cost anything, is there a limit?
costs.a:
Using it costs you nothing.

Part of the models run through KISSKI at GWDG, under a strict quota shared across the whole university: 2 requests per second, 15 per minute, 900 per hour, 21,000 per day and 350,000 per month. If other people have that quota busy right now, a request can come back with an error.

THL myLab, the second provider, has no fixed limit at the moment. On the second Thursday of each month from 8 pm, its systems get updated, and it can be unreachable during that window.

gdpr.q: Is my data safe and GDPR-compliant?
gdpr.a:
Yes. Processing happens at THL myLab, GWDG/KISSKI and DeepL, all in Germany or the EU. None of them train on the data.

What is stored in detail, and for how long, is set out in the privacy policy.

hosting.q: Who runs the platform, where are the servers?
hosting.a: The platform runs at Hetzner in Germany, uploaded files are held in Hetzner Object Storage.

models.q: Which AI models are used and who decides that?
models.a:
The KIS team configures the models centrally. They run at three providers: THL myLab at TH Lübeck, KISSKI from GWDG in Göttingen, and DeepL for translating files.

In the chat with the learning assistant, gemma4-31b answers. Which model sits behind the other services changes from time to time. When a service has more than one provider set up, for example translation, text to audio or the image generator, you pick it yourself in the form.

whoSees.q: Who can see my materials and my chat?
whoSees.a: Materials and chat belong to the workspace and are visible to its members. A small circle of people with the corresponding permission may inspect them for technical support, as set out in the privacy policy.

afterPilot.q: What happens to my data once the pilot project ends?
afterPilot.a: At the latest when the pilot project ends, your workspaces and uploaded files are deleted. If you want that sooner, send us an email or a message through the feedback form.

notFound.q: Why does the learning assistant not know something that is in the document?
notFound.a:
The learning assistant does not search a whole document at once, he searches it in sections. If the answer is spread across many places, or sits only in a table or a graphic, he may not find it.

What helps: narrow the question, name the chapter, or leave only that one document active in the source selection.

generalQuestions.q: Why does he not answer general questions?
generalQuestions.a: That is deliberate. The learning assistant is tied to the materials of the workspace so that nothing enters an answer that is not in them. He is not meant for anything else.

trust.q: Can I trust the answers, and what are the sources on each sentence for?
trust.a: The small sources behind a sentence lead to the spot in the document it came from. One click opens and highlights it. Use them to check anything that matters, AI answers can be wrong.

studentView.q: What do students see when I give them access to a workspace?
studentView.a: Materials, chat and the tools in the studio. Not visible are the workspace settings, the participant management and the figures for the whole workspace. You can check this yourself in the student view.

bugReport.q: Where do I report a problem?
bugReport.a: Through the feedback form. Say what you did and what happened, that saves a follow-up question.

presentationTemplate.q: What does my own template need for the presentation service?
presentationTemplate.a: A pptx or potx file up to 30 MB without macros. The first slide master counts. Layouts need a heading, otherwise they are skipped. Image fields are needed for images to be created. The image style is described in English.

what.a: KIS stands for Kinternationalisierung von Studiengängen, the internationalisation of degree programmes. It is a funded pilot project at THL meant to support international students starting a degree taught in German. At the same time, KIS is a transfer project: what is developed in the pilot is meant to be transferable to other degree programmes and other universities.

how.q: How does working with the platform work?
how.a: Teachers have services such as screencast, podcast or presentation and also the learning assistant. Teachers create a workspace, upload documents and other materials and manage them. Then they invite students. The students work with the material in the workspace and ask Francis their questions about it. During the pilot phase the services are available to teachers only. Technically it would be possible to open them to students as well in the future.

state.a: KIS is in its pilot phase in the Electrical Engineering degree programme. The platform is being tested and developed further, some functions may still change.

who.q: Who can use the platform, and can I try it?
who.a: Currently it is not generally accessible. Access is planned for a group of students for testing and for further test users. If you would like to try it, write to us via the contact at the end of the page. We will look together at whether and how a test is possible in your case.

sources.q: Where does Francis get its answers?
sources.a: Francis answers from the sources in your workspace.

names.q: How do I know what an answer is based on?
names.a: Francis names the source for every answer so you can read up on it.

dsgvo.a: Yes. The platform is built so that only GDPR compliant services are used. Teachers who connect a voice service of their own do so with their own account and at their own responsibility.

hosting.a: The platform is operated by the project team at THL and runs on servers in Germany. The AI models run on infrastructure of THL and of partners in Germany.

after.q: What happens after the pilot phase?
after.a: Afterwards the project is meant to be transferred to further degree programmes. How exactly is decided by THL after the evaluation.

integration.q: Will the platform be connected to Moodle and the THL account?
integration.a: This is in progress. Signing in via SSO is planned, and a connection to Moodle via LTI is being considered for the future.

services.heading: Services for teachers
services.intro: Besides the learning assistant, teachers find these services right on the start page.

translation.lead: Translates texts and documents between German and English. A presentation stays a presentation, layout and formatting are kept.
translation.p1: Type text directly or upload a file, such as Word, PowerPoint or Markdown
translation.p2: The source language is detected automatically
translation.p3: Glossaries let you decide how technical terms are translated
translation.alt: Translation with text input, target language and glossary selection

tts.lead: Reads texts and documents aloud with natural sounding voices. The result is an MP3 file.
tts.p1: Type text or upload a file
tts.p2: Listen to voices first and pick the one that fits
tts.p3: Long texts are voiced in pieces, finished pieces are kept if a job is stopped
tts.alt: Text to audio with text input, provider and voice

transcription.lead: Transcribes audio and video, either as plain text or as subtitles with timestamps.
transcription.p1: Common audio and video formats are supported
transcription.p2: Output as text, SRT or VTT
transcription.p3: The transcript can be edited before you download it
transcription.alt: Audio to text with file selection and output format

summary.lead: Combines several materials into one text, as a short briefing, study guide or timeline.
summary.p1: Up to ten files or materials from a workspace
summary.p2: An instruction narrows down a topic or shapes the text
summary.p3: The template decides how the text is structured
summary.alt: Report with sources, template and instruction

podcast.lead: Your material becomes a conversation to listen to. You choose content and cast, check the script and have it voiced.
podcast.p1: One to four speakers, each with a role and a voice
podcast.p2: Length of about 5 to 20 minutes, style explanatory, casual or as an interview
podcast.p3: The result is an MP3 file, the transcript comes with it
podcast.alt: Podcast with source selection, language and instruction

praesentation.lead: Your material becomes slides in the university design, with images, tables and charts where the template provides for them.
praesentation.p1: The outline comes first for you to rearrange, then the slides
praesentation.p2: The THL template is preset, your own template can be uploaded
praesentation.p3: The result is a PowerPoint file, with speaker notes if you like
praesentation.alt: Presentation with source selection and slide master

screencast.lead: Turns a PowerPoint file into a narrated video, in another language if you like.
screencast.p1: The narration comes from the slides, from an import or from the notes of the file
screencast.p2: You can check and edit every narration text or have a new one suggested
screencast.p3: The video is available as MP4, with subtitles if you like
screencast.alt: Screencast with file upload and target language

image.lead: Create images, adapt existing images or have them described. Every result becomes the starting point for the next step.
image.p1: Styles such as photo, illustration or THL slide style and several formats
image.p2: Up to four variants at once
image.p3: Images are created without text by default because image models often misspell words
image.alt: Image generation with prompt, style and format

glossary.lead: Here you keep your own term lists so that technical terms are translated the same way everywhere.
glossary.p1: An entry consists of the German and the English term
glossary.p2: The glossary takes effect in translation and screencast
glossary.p3: Glossaries can be exported and passed on to colleagues
glossary.alt: Glossary with the list of your own term lists

pages.lead: Your material becomes a learning page with pictures, tables and charts that you can share and add to a workspace.
pages.p1: The AI itself picks which forms fit the material, such as pictures, tables or a mind map
pages.p2: Every text, picture and label can be edited afterwards
pages.p3: Share by link, with or without a KIS account
pages.alt: Pages overview with one finished learning page
